source.title: Advancing Spiking Neural Networks towards Deep Residual Learning
source.authors: Yifan Hu; Lei Deng; Yu-Jie Wu; Man Yao; Guo-Qi Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. It includes flattened tables and figures whose exact plotted values are not available in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests depth and shortcut behavior in directly trained spiking networks, extending the depth question to SNNs and an SNN-specific residual design.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 depth results in Table II and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 alternative-structure results in Table VI. It also describes training and test accuracy degradation, but reports no numeric training-error values. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study investigates optimization in directly trained LIF spiking networks, rather than the conventional networks specified by these versions. Its depth tables report test accuracy, which cannot establish V3's training-error effect. Its initialization experiments concern residual-path BN scales, rather than V4's activation-matched initialization in plain networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors attribute vanilla spiking ResNet degradation to unavailing residual representations and unstable gradients associated with interblock LIF. Their membrane-shortcut design mitigates this problem and enables directly trained SNNs with 482 layers on CIFAR-10 and 104 layers on ImageNet.
record.recipe_differences: Direct surrogate-gradient SNN training with LIF neurons and temporal backpropagation; the proposed membrane shortcut removes interblock LIF and adds LIF at residual-path tops.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and residual-block design change accuracy; in MS-ResNet, setting residual-path γ2 to zero accelerates convergence, while setting γ1 near zero has the opposite effect.

fits_no_version.finding: In directly trained LIF spiking networks, PlainNet test accuracy peaks at 14 layers and vanilla ResNet at 20 layers, then declines. Removing interblock LIF permits increasing accuracy through 56 layers. MS-ResNet reaches 91.7% and 91.9% test accuracy at 110 and 482 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth degradation in directly trained spiking convolutional networks depends on residual-block design; membrane shortcuts without interblock LIF permit much deeper training.

fits_no_version.finding: All three alternative spiking shortcut structures improve test accuracy between 32 and 110 layers on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under the Table VI recipe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several spiking residual structures with uninterrupted identity pathways avoid test-accuracy degradation over the tested depths.

fits_no_version.finding: The introduction and Section V.A explicitly report declining training as well as test accuracy with depth in vanilla spiking ResNet. The proposed structure avoids the reported degradation; numeric training-error depth comparisons are unavailable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vanilla residual blocks can suffer training degradation in directly trained SNNs, and removing interblock LIF alleviates it.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing the second residual-path BN scale accelerates MS-ResNet convergence with standard BN and TDBN, including improving a non-convergent 104-layer case. Initializing the first BN scale near zero has the opposite effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-path BN scale initialization controls early convergence in MS-ResNet, with different effects depending on which BN scale is reduced.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The depth analysis uses relatively narrow architectures and is explicitly focused on depth response rather than state-of-the-art results. Table II and Table VI report accuracy, not training error. Initialization values in Figure 5 are figure-only in the supplied text. The paper notes overfitting in MS-ResNet104 and limited regularization in deep CIFAR-10 results.
record.rows_left_out: None. All extracted depth rows and the two initialization findings are included.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in conventional CIFAR convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation and its prevention in the conventional networks specified; longer-training controls, deep plain tanh initialization, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth of plain convolutional networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness evolution, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The SNN results are relevant analogues, but do not establish or refute the versions as written. The paper's explicit qualitative training-accuracy statements should be retained alongside its test-accuracy tables. Standard BN versus TDBN is not normalization versus no normalization. Untested initialization mechanisms do not warrant a limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error results for CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, and no corrupted or random-label results.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU experiments or student-width sweep.

Tests directly trained SNNs, not conventional ANN networks; reports accuracy rather than numeric training error. The deep plain-network special-initialization and normalization-free residual cases in the version are not evaluated.

Tests residual-path BN scale initialization in MS-ResNet; does not test activation-matched initializations, plain tanh networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiments.
Does not compare batch normalization against no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: MS-ResNet at first epoch
rows.operation_detail: Compared residual-path BN scale initializations; Figure 5 reports first-epoch accuracy.
rows.measure: accuracy after first epoch and training convergence
rows.note: Text says γ2=0 significantly accelerates convergence for standard BN and TDBN.
rows.check: The text establishes faster convergence from zeroing residual-path γ2 in MS-ResNet, but this is outside V4's plain-network initialization claim.

rows.subject: MS-ResNet104
rows.operation_detail: Compared residual-path BN scale initialization; Figure 5 shows training loss curves.
rows.note: Text says the 104-layer model has one non-convergent case that is radically improved by setting γ2 to zero.
rows.check: This is a residual spiking-network initialization result outside V4. Standard BN shows no training-loss decrease over ten epochs; zeroing γ2 substantially improves convergence, rather than demonstrating a partial V4 effect.

relation.reason: The paper discusses conventional-network residual learning and initialization as motivation, but its own results concern spiking-network architectures and do not test the stated versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments concern directly trained LIF spiking networks, outside the systems specified by the claim versions. The sampled depth results measure test accuracy; the initialization experiments vary residual-path BN scales rather than testing V4's activation-matched initialization claims.

source_check.notes: The authors also describe degradation in training accuracy, but the sampled tables report test accuracy. The supplied source is arXiv v3 dated 10 March 2023; the record uses the original 2021 year.
